28590: The eldest daughter of the Archduke of Springland, hailed as "Springland's Winter Jasmine" and a dazzling new star in the empire's elite social circles. Raised with familial affection and public admiration, Vera's privileged upbringing and elite education endowed her with graceful manners and impeccable aristocratic poise. From royalty to the six Archduke houses, all desired a daughter-in-law as noble and gentle as Vera. The Archduke of Springland repeatedly declined marriage proposals at every banquet, while Vera mastered the art of elegantly turning down endless suitors. Though agriculturally-rooted Springland upheld tradition, its Archduke remained progressive—rejecting rigid etiquette to let his daughter flourish like "wildflowers in an open field." Yet Vera's innate warmth and diligence led her to voluntarily embrace noble duties: accompanying her father through intricate social affairs, mediating disputes among temperamental aristocrats. Her radiant smile and melodious voice proved the ultimate peacemaker—even the roughest generals softened under Vera's gaze. #r As the Emperor's confidant and Imperial Clan Court Chancellor, the Archduke navigated the empire's complex power dynamics. Inheriting his talents, the mature Vera joined the Imperial Clan Court, assisting in managing noble relations. Beyond diplomatic finesse, she possessed rare mana affinity, studying ancient astrology under Holy Elves Mages—knowledge even revered among elves. Surprisingly, Vera—warm as March sunshine—was blessed not by the pure "White Moon" star symbolizing HP and sanctity, but by the fierce comet "Shadow Sun", representing destructive magic in astrological lore. Thus, despite a decade of training, she treated magic as a hobby, never wielding its power—fearing harm to others and the unleashing of her own buried wildness. #r When dire news arrived from the west, unease gripped the Imperial Clan Court. Vera sensed war and conspiracy in the tension, her heart aching at her father's exhaustion. Unexpectedly, this diplomatic novice was dispatched as envoy to western Chen-Yuan for border trade talks. As her father entrusted her with a long-sealed emerald Codex, Vera understood the mission's gravity. Though Fear, anxiety, and helplessness gripped her, she revealed nothing. With imperial currents turning treacherous and her Family at stake, maintaining her flawless Character became vital to avoid burdening her father. Suppressing inner turmoil, "Springland's Winter Jasmine" journeyed westward as the "Shadow Sun" Burned across the void above. #r The stars had woven her fate: spring might end, yet the Winter Jasmine would keep blooming—layering summer, autumn, and winter hues—standing vibrant in the new era.
28591: The era never lacks Heroes or Normal folk—those awaiting rescue in epics or serving as stepping stones in tales. To them, the "drama" bards sing of means shattered lives and life savings turned to ash. They cheer Heroes with flowers at the end, as if their own homes and futures weren't lost. So Aya Novian never wished to be a Hero. To her, those flashy-caped Jokers were show-offs chasing fame, likely never starved or scorned, utterly unable to empathize with Normal people. From childhood, Aya knew: she had no Ability or right to save anyone. Even if she did, what was the point? Morality was a full-belly pastime; generosity, jewelry for the high and mighty. Fine things—but not for a slum-raised girl. Aya never learned her father's fate—drunk in a gutter or mugged by slum thieves. Seeing her mother's swollen eyes and twisted face before she left, Aya knew she'd never return. Routine in the lower district. Guards sealed their shack, dumping her at a nunnery—a kind soul raising unwanted kids.#r Nunnery life was neither good nor bad. The old nun stretched meager donations to feed them, with no energy left for their spirits. Aya ran wild with older kids, pulling rough pranks, burning off restless energy, learning the slums' rules through endless lies and fights. Piety, integrity, and Good earned no bread. What filled bellies? Well-timed theft, cunning scams, and fists like stones.#r When Aya grew old enough to lead, the nunnery fell—Sunrise Sect rose as The Rising faith's core. The Dawn Lady's nun was cast out with her crumbling chapel. What did piety, integrity, and Good buy? No flock, no zeal, few taxes—not even thanks. Praying before the renovated chapel's holy flames, her thin frame and lonely shadow killed Aya's last hope for the world. Only helpless children endured the new priest's harsh rules; the rest returned to vagrant life. Cornered, Aya joined the army as a Redpineland frontline Bow archer. Discipline choked her free spirit. After two years, over a kept trophy, she deserted, sold it black-market—three days' profit topped six months' pay.#r Taste for profit, Aya dodged pursuit to Burningland—the wildest frontier, ripe with chances. Here, only her Bow and blade mattered. With top Ability and no rules, she rose fast, a legend in the Hummingbird Guild. Morals? Rules? Rep? Worthless. For the right price, her Bow and blade handled any dirty task. None knew where her Ducats went. Rumors claimed she splurged inland between jobs. Aya stayed silent.#r Back home, the old nun rented rooms opposite the chapel, tending orphans without preaching her Deity. Across the street, the gold-plated The Rising Statue loomed, holy flames blazing yet colder than her dim window's glow. Whispers: she embezzled funds to afford it. Or: she was a count's heir, collecting monthly money orders. No one linked this to the fierce, troublemaking girl. Aya prayed they wouldn't. She Opposed the nun's piety, integrity, and Good—but secretly wished others would believe it for her.#r The world drowns in shadows—yet must keep lights lit, for children still fighting the dark.

28686:
Beyond obscure texts and the crumbling King's Rest Place, the Ancient Empire left nothing. King Kurulek's The Sins and glory have dimmed; his people are no longer the mighty Legion facing storms head-on, but now struggle as desert folk in raging sands. History is Bato's sole pride—they cling to proof of past greatness: history, knowledge, ruins, royal tombs. 

 On the sand sea, the dynasty feeds Bato, the great library nourishes their minds, The Order of Veil strengthens their spirit. The Order witnesses Bato's death, using it to give life meaning. To Bato, death is a sacred rite to enter history—holy, an honor shared with noble ancestors. All tied to the ancient dynasty is sacred, Protected by the Order's laws and royal decrees, especially tombs. Desecrate the dead, and you Desecrate the race; evildoers pay. 

 Salem is that punishment. 

 The Order of Veil lacks strict ranks; Salem is simply Salem—name or Position, unknown. Like all acolytes, he's lived in the Order since childhood. His parents? Ruling nobles or heroic devotees; only the most loyal's children may join. Salem's path was smooth: studying history, rituals, preserving relics, then mastering Ancient Empire combat arts. Truthfully, he dislikes fighting—feels no thrill, only duty. Grave Scorpion's aid has limits; the Order needs someone for vital Missions, and Salem is uniquely gifted. 

 Off-duty, Salem delves into dynastic history: Ancient Empire epics, kingly tales, pottery and sickle-shaped swords decaying in howling winds. Without his scars and calluses, he'd pass as a librarian, not the feared Messenger of the Sandstorm—an Order Warrior striking fear into grave robbers and black marketeers. His proudest knowledge stays hidden; people recall only his iconic arm guards and sickle-shaped sword. Well, two relics fit a monument guardian. 

 Those Weapons are Salem's medals too, once wielded by the glorious Ushak Legion—"guardians," King Kurulek's elite. Sand-eroded and rusted shut, they can no longer unfold into shields per Ancient Scripture. Stolen by greedy Caucaid adventurers from a Sasin general's tomb, they reached a count. Their crime? Conspiring to kill a priest, posing as aides, ambushing a funeral, looting tombs, slaughtering unarmed priests—Salem's own temple. 

 Salem missed the funeral; his grin died that day. He rode the sands from Great Sand Sea to Caucaid. Sand sweeps sin; Salem casts sinners into it. Four years later, he reclaimed the relics then spared the count—the sand's rage eased; the count merely bought antiques at auction. 

 The avenger returned; Hostile cleansed by duty. The Order gave him the relics, making him Last Ushak: forebears guarded kings, he guards their legacy. Salem stays the cheerful priest—but to those daring to Desecrate Bato's history, he's their last sight.
28687: Captain of the Li-Shan Army and commander of the Liuyun Cavalry, Xu Zhao is a young Bei-Ting faction Commander and trusted aide of Protector-General Yuchi An. Known for his Trait of sternness and extreme discipline, he stands apart from his straightforward Bei-Ting comrades. Though often absent from banquets and games, Xu Zhao is regarded by his peers as a dependable ally. Despite his rank, he lives like an ordinary Soldier—eschewing official connections and scholarly pursuits. No strategic mastermind, he knows his strengths lie elsewhere: as Bei-Ting's Silence spear tip, he charges unreservedly toward the deadliest fronts. #r Veterans often note how Xu Zhao mirrors his father. Hailing from prosperous Nan-Xi, his grandfather settled in Bei-Ting after Xuan-Lin's Northern Expedition, earning land through valor during the Circle of Calamity Neutral. His father joined the Loong-Town Guardian Troop as the Family wished, retiring after decades of service due to injury. Xu Zhao then took up his father's blade and enlisted in the Li-Shan Army. Without grand ideals or authorities' summons, generations of borderland men have stepped forward to man the walls guarding their homeland for centuries. Nan-Xi's fishing songs and Bei-Ting's war drums—both are rhythms of life. While Chen-Yuan's people choose their paths, someone must ever keep watch atop these walls. #r To Xu Zhao, Bei-Ting is everything—even above his own HP. Raised on tales of countless Heroes and tempered by loss, his fervent patriotism is his creed, surpassing scholarly debates or rigid hierarchies. When the Li-Shan Army left Bei-Ting for Wu-Wei under the Protector-General's orders, Xu Zhao hesitated, even considering transfer to Loong City. Yet after a lengthy talk with his commander, he Silencely obeyed. Though unclear about court intrigues, he trusts Yuchi An—a lifelong soldier whose love for Bei-Ting matches his own. For Bei-Ting's peace and Loong City's survival, Xu Zhao will remain that silent spear tip, even if it breaks. Where conflict breeds war, war demands Sacrifice—personal glory pales when weighed against Bei-Ting's future.
28688: To embrace the warmth of The Rising is to endure its scorch. Not even a Deity can alter nature's law: light and shadow are twins. #r In the Chamber of Rising Sun, Torchbearers are pariahs. Their extremist views and blind zeal allow no flexibility. Their fanatic preaching and rigid orthodoxy make them unstable fireballs, igniting clashes between church and state. Even internally, peace is scarce—extremists deem all others lukewarm, living by the creed: "No piety but absolute." #r Thus Torchbearers wander alone, drifting on paranoid pilgrimages toward doom through hollow sermons. These robed eccentrics clutch eternal flames, obsessed with eradicating every shadow. Ironically, they shackle the church itself—preventing local parishes from growing corrupt by colluding with secular powers and forgetting their duty as servants of The Rising. As the Chamber of Rising Sun's influence swells, the entire faith grows feverish—especially the already radical Torchbearers. They turn their gaze beyond the church, leading Fanatical Believer gangs along the borderlands, their atrocities becoming legend. In this climate, the "timeworn" ways of "White Flame" Kane seem out of step, marking him a heretic among peers. #r Becoming a Torchbearer begins by burning one's past—so Kane Sunflare's origins remain obscure. In an age where holy fire burns mad, his crusade against internal rot has brought infamy. Rumors hold that before converting to Lady of The Rising, he was a renowned Mage in the Spire. His peerless The Rising Prayer owes much to his arcane roots. Kane lives by a Torchbearer's oath: a solitary path shunning vanity, ignoring the Church, interpreting faith solely through ancient texts. His epithet stems from his signature act—investigating local Area churches and burning those he judges "corrupt." #r Torchbearers claim true understanding of Lady of The Rising, but Kane's reading of The Rising Tome skews extreme. He adheres to "Inner Radiance"—teaching that chanting The Rising's name proves nothing; true devotion lies in living by Her virtues, whether one speaks Her name or not. The HEARTFLAME school began moderately, but Kane ignores human frailty, demanding divine discipline from all. He calls himself a necessary evil—the sear endured to embrace The Rising. Unlike fanatic peers, he owns his zeal, justifying it through lore, bearing it with self-Sacrifice martyrdom. His logic is sound: zeal breeds blindness, blindness distorts, distortion corrupts—and he is The Rising's purging flame. Yet the uneasy high priests cry heresy: they convict him for three bishops' deaths and exile him for life. #r The sentence barely stings—Torchbearers exile themselves regardless. But with the Church's stance, Kane's probes into local church misconduct grow thorny. With no alternative, he journeys to Burningland, home of the Chamber of Rising Sun, shouldering another Torchbearer duty: spreading the faith. Countless souls in the west thirst for light—and Sunrise Bishop Godwin reeks of scandal. Kane must unearth secrets buried beneath this soil, ensuring this golden branch won't fester.
